We'll start with the table from part 3.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $4$ | $1$ |

We now proceed to approximate $y(\frac{3}{2})$ using Euler's method.

**Step 1.** We compute the values of ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and ${y}_{\text{new}}$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=1+\frac{1}{4}=\frac{5}{4} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy=2+1=3\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $4$ | $1$ |
| $\frac{5}{4}$ | $3$ | $$ | $$ |

**Step 2.** We compute ${y}^{′}$ and $Δy$ (using the values of $x$ and $y$ in the second row) and new values of ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and ${y}_{\text{new}}$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =x{y}^{2}=\frac{5}{4}\cdot {3}^{2}=\frac{45}{4} \\ Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx=\frac{45}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{4}=\frac{45}{16} \\ {x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=\frac{5}{4}+\frac{1}{4}=\frac{3}{2} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy=3+\frac{45}{16}=\frac{93}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $4$ | $1$ |
| $\frac{5}{4}$ | $3$ | $\frac{45}{4}$ | $\frac{45}{16}$ |
| $\frac{3}{2}$ | $\frac{93}{16}$ | $$ | $$ |

Therefore, we conclude that $y(\frac{3}{2})≈\frac{93}{16}.$
